body:
## Problem

The v0.77.0 tag still hardcodes vendor model IDs in production routing code, contrary to the live-catalog requirement behind #77/#109:

- `src/model_catalog.rs::fallback_models` seeds Claude, Codex, Gemini and Qwen with fixed model arrays such as `claude-opus-4-7`, `gpt-5-codex`, `gemini-2.5-pro`, `qwen3-coder-plus` and marks them `using_fallback`;
- `src/anthropic_bridge.rs::resolve_bridge_model` hardcodes `gpt-5-codex`, `qwen3-coder-plus` and Gemini `DEFAULT_MODEL` when no bridge override is set.

The live Codex catalog observed through v0.77 contains eight current IDs and does not contain `gpt-5-codex`, so the built-in bridge default is already outside the provider list. Hardcoded fallbacks can advertise or route to models that are unavailable, renamed, withdrawn, not entitled, or never authorized.

## Expected behavior

- Start every subscription catalog empty/unavailable until a successful authenticated live discovery for that exact account.
- Persist the last successful catalog with account identity, fetched time and explicit health, but never seed it from source-code model names.
- Do not expose persisted models while the credential is missing/revoked; expose degradation separately to admins.
- Resolve a missing cross-protocol bridge model from the healthy account live catalog and capability metadata, with a deterministic operator-configurable policy (for example cheapest compatible/default advertised model).
- Reject with a clear `model_selection_required`/provider-unavailable error when no compatible live model exists; never silently substitute a source-code constant.
- Namespace collisions by provider/account and preserve requested/resolved identity and attribution in every response.
- Client setup/default selection must query the authenticated union catalog at execution time, not embed known model IDs.
- Add tests with entirely synthetic future model names and zero familiar GPT/Claude/Gemini/Qwen names, proving catalog, routing, bridge selection and clients still work.
title: Remove hardcoded model catalogs and bridge defaults; derive all routing from live provider catalogs
